rationale.conceptual: The work uses widespread DFT+Transport methodology with a well-known functional (TB-mBJ) and a routine calibration step; no new algorithms or deep mathematical derivations are involved.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has 4 sequential stages (structural relaxation, band structure, Boltzmann transport, calibration) with dependencies between them and requires installation of two specialized CPU-based codes (exciting and BoltzTraP2) and retrieval of one experimental data point from a paper.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies standard DFT (GGA and TB-mBJ functionals) and semi-classical Boltzmann transport to SnO2, a simple material, without novel algorithms. The pipeline involves structural relaxation, electronic structure calculation, Boltzmann transport integration, and relaxation-time calibration against one experimental data point. Conceptual difficulty is low (standard method with a minor functional variation), execution requires a 4-step pipeline with tooling (exciting, BoltzTraP2) and a small external data fetch, placing it at the lower end of multi-stage complexity.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT calculations on a small unit cell (SnO2, 6 atoms) with ~1000 k-points and moderate FP-LAPW settings (RMT*KMAX=7) are CPU-bound and require a few GB of RAM; no large datasets or GPU acceleration needed.
